label: lem:antiderivatives_diff_constant
title: Antiderivatives differ by a constant
statement: If $a \le b$ and $F, G$ are both continuous antiderivatives of $f$ on $(a,b)$, then $F - G$ is constant on $[a,b]$: for all $x \in [a,b]$, $(F - G)(x) = (F - G)(a)$.
proof: By Lemma~\ref{lem:antideriv_diff_zero_deriv}, $F - G$ has zero derivative on $(a,b)$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:zero_deriv_constant}, it is constant.
